citation: Hammerson, G.A., Frost, D.R. & Gadsden, H. 2019. Phrynosoma platyrhinos. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2019: e.T89974770A89975571. Accessed on 05 May 2026.

actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species occurs widely in the west of the United States, extending into northwestern Mexico. The range extends from southeastern Oregon, southwestern Idaho, and northern Utah south through eastern and southern California, Nevada, and western Arizona to a portion of northeastern Baja California (Pianka 1991, Grismer 2002, St. John 2002, Stebbins 2003, Mulcahy et al. 2006). Old records for northeastern Utah need verification (St. John 2002). Populations south of the Gila River in southwestern Arizona and northwestern Sonora, Mexico (formerly included in P. platyrhinos), are now recognized as a distinct species, Phrynosoma goodei (Mulcahy et al. 2006). Elevational range extends from below sea level (desert sinks) to about 1,980 m (Stebbins 2003). The species is represented by a large number of collection sites (Pianka 1991); populations probably are extant in most of these localities.
documentation.population: This species is very common for a horned lizard. The total adult population size is unknown but is certainly very large (> 100,000). Extent of occurrence, area of occupancy, and population size are probably relatively stable or slowly declining.
documentation.habitats: This lizard inhabits all sorts of desert shrublands, such as those dominated by Sagebrush, Shadscale, Hopsage, Creosotebush, or Greasewood, on sandy flats, alluvial fans, washes, or brushy dunes or dune edges (Grismer 2002, St. John 2002, Stebbins 2003). It is most consistently found where areas of bare ground exist among openly spaced shrubs. It occurs where summers are hot and winters are cold or mild; winter temperatures generally are too cold for activity.
documentation.threats: No major threats have been identified. Locally, subpopulations have been reduced or eliminated as a result of urbanization, agricultural development, and off-road vehicle use.
documentation.measures: Subpopulations exist in several national parks, monuments, and wilderness areas.
documentation.use_trade: Individuals are collected for the pet trade or as curiosities. Most of these die in captivity or are released in sites other than the collection site.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, large number of locations, presumed large population, and because it is unlikely to be declining fast enough to qualify for listing in a more threatened category.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: Mulcahy et al. (2006) examined phylogeography of Phrynosoma in the vicinity of the Salton Trough of southern California and northwestern Mexico and concluded that three species occur there: Phrynoma mcallii (endemic to the trough), P. goodei (which previously was recognized as a subspecies of P. platyrhinos; east of the Colorado River and south of the Gila River), and P. platyrhinos (elsewhere in the region).
